rationale: Successor experiment for 0bfc2ea5a9e94316982943d306eefbf6-question-0, pursuing a concrete unobserved consequence of the recorded wedge fact: whether the wedged replica removes the cluster's one-failure tolerance. The harness keeps the two truncation subtests exactly as they were (so the receipt 2086b09f107d4d49b1407754feabb781 stays valid for the conditions it witnessed) and appends an escalation phase that runs in both modes: after the wedge window, the remaining healthy voter is removed at the transport level and the leader applies one new client entry while the leader's commit index, its apply future and both nodes' probes are sampled for 1500 ms. A three-voter cluster is expected to keep committing with one voter down, so the control shows what the history yields without the store error; running the same phase in the faulted mode makes the discrimination direct. Native local feedback on this harness in a scratch copy inside draft showed the expected split, but the retained execution decides.

experiment.revision_reason: Same investigation and same truncation staging, extended with a peer-loss escalation phase that runs in both the control and the faulted mode and is observed with a new receipt; the earlier receipt remains the witness for the truncation windows it recorded.

scope.description: Two subtests, control and injected_store_error, each building three voters from the library's own in-memory components with a legal fault-injecting LogStore wrapper on the node that becomes the initial leader, running the legal partition/divergence/higher-term-replacement history, healing, sampling the certificate and store for 1500 ms, removing the fault and sampling once more after 1200 ms. Then the escalation phase, identical in both subtests: the current leader is located, the remaining healthy voter is disconnected in both directions, one client entry is applied on the leader, and for 1500 ms the leader's commit index, whether the returned future completes, its error, the leader's and the wedged node's certificate/store probes and every node's state and term are recorded.
assumptions: A LogStore returning an error from StoreLogs is an allowed outcome of the interface, not corruption of an acknowledged durable write; the wrapper returns the error without touching the underlying store.

The staged history is a legal single-cluster history: the tail entries the diverging node holds were appended while it was isolated and were never committed, and the majority's replacement entries are committed at a higher term.
Three voters with one removed is the failure the configuration is expected to tolerate, so a stalled commit in that state is meaningful rather than an artifact of the setup.
In-memory LoopbackTransport delivers RPCs in-process without loss, so nonprogress is produced by the library's logic rather than by transport faults.
excluded: No production code is modified; the wrapper implements the public LogStore interface only.
No restart, snapshot install or leader-side compaction is performed, so those repair paths remain unexecuted in this experiment.

experiment.prefix: Each subtest prints CA_EVENT lines: truncation_before_heal, truncation_after_heal (with cert_index_samples, store_last_samples and store_attempts), truncation_after_disarm, and the new peer_loss_after_wedge carrying removed_voter, leader, leader_state, leader_term, commit_before, commit_samples (25 ms interval, 1500 ms), apply_future_done, apply_future_error, leader_probe, wedged_node_probe and state_and_term.
